evidence.summary: At cycle 174, filter differential pressure (filter_dp_bar) rose to 0.467 bar (+13.1% vs baseline 0.413 bar, z=1.7). Coolant flow decreased to 38.8 L/min (-3.7% vs baseline 40.3 L/min). Outlet pressure fell to 4.496 bar (-1.6% vs baseline 4.569 bar). Inlet pressure remained near baseline.
Remaining useful life estimated at 76 cycles, policy band 'above_50_monitor' indicating monitoring but not immediate failure.

SOP-C-202 describes filter differential pressure above 0.7 bar and rising, with outlet pressure falling while inlet pressure stays normal, and coolant flow dropping as symptoms of coolant filter clog.
High filter differential pressure with normal inlet pressure indicates cartridge loading with swarf, consistent with observed sensor pattern.

report.summary: Unit U024 showed a significant rise in filter differential pressure (13% above baseline) together with a drop in coolant flow and outlet pressure, while inlet pressure remained stable. These sensor deviations match the symptom profile for a coolant filter clog as defined in SOP-C-202. The unit's RUL is still adequate (76 cycles remaining), so immediate replacement of the filter is recommended to prevent further performance degradation.
